chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, he raised it (to the Imam), he said:
"When a gift of food is presented to a man and there are people with him, they are his partners in it; the fruit and other than it."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sharing received food gifts with those present?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling within the chapter on earnings (*al-Makasib*), emphasizing that the presence of companions transforms a private gift into a communal obligation of generosity. This principle extends beyond formal feasts to include fruits and other consumables, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social equity and the moral duty to share blessings with those in one's immediate circle.
